readings.title: Job Rebukes the Accusers
readings.subtitle: A Demand for Right-Ruling
readings.text: [Job 13:1] “Look, my eye has seen it all, my ear has heard and understood it. [2] What you know, I know too; I am not less than you. [3] But I would speak to the <dn>Almighty</dn>, and I delight to reason with <dn>Ěl</dn>. [4] But you smear with falsehood, worthless healers, all of you! [5] If you would only be silent, then it would be your wisdom! [6] Please hear my reasoning, and listen to the pleadings of my lips. [7] Would you speak perversely for <dn>Ěl</dn>, and speak deceit for <dn>Him</dn>? [8] Would you be partial towards <dn>Him</dn>? Would you plead for <dn>Ěl</dn>? [9] Would it be well when <dn>He</dn> searches <dn>את</dn> you out? Or could you deceive <dn>Him</dn> as one deceives a man? [10] <dn>He</dn> would certainly reprove <dn>את</dn> you if you secretly show partiality. [11] Should not <dn>His</dn> excellence make <dn>את</dn> you afraid, and the dread of <dn>Him</dn> fall upon you? [12] Your weighty sayings are proverbs of ashes, your shields are shields of clay. [13] Be silent before me, and let me speak, and let whatever come upon me! [14] Why do I take my flesh in my teeth, and put my life in my hands? [15] Though, <dn>He</dn> kills· me – in <dn>Him</dn> I expect! But I show my ways to be right before <dn>Him</dn>. [16] <dn>He</dn> also is my deliverance, for a defiled one does not come before <dn>Him</dn>. [17] Listen closely to my words, and with your ears to what I say. [18] Look, please, I have prepared my case, I know that I am in the right. [19] Who is he who would strive with me? For then I would keep silent and die.

readings.title: The Frailty of the Flesh
readings.subtitle: A Plea for the Premial Verdict
readings.text: [Job 13:20] Only two matters do not do to me, then I am not hidden from <dn>Your</dn> face: [21] Withdraw <dn>Your</dn> hand far from me, and let not dread of <dn>You</dn> make me afraid. [22] Then call, and let me answer; or let me speak, and <dn>You</dn> reply to me. [23] How many are my crookednesses and sins? Let me know my transgression and my sin. [24] Why do <dn>You</dn> hide <dn>Your</dn> face, and reckon me as <dn>Your</dn> enemy? [25] Would <dn>You</dn> frighten a leaf driven to and fro? And would <dn>You</dn> pursue <dn>את</dn> dry stubble? [26] For <dn>You</dn> write bitter charges against me, and make me inherit the crookednesses of my youth, [27] and put my feet in the stocks, and look closely to <dn>את</dn> all my paths. <dn>You</dn> set a limit for the soles of my feet. [28] And he, like that which is rotten, wastes away, as a garment that is moth-eaten. [Job 14:1] “Man born of woman is of few days and turmoil-filled. [2] He comes forth like a flower and withers. He flees like a shadow and does not continue. [3] Yet on such a one <dn>You</dn> open <dn>Your</dn> eyes, and bring <dn>את</dn> me to right-ruling with <dn>Yourself</dn>! [4] Who brings the clean out of the unclean? No one! [5] Since his days are decided, the number of his new moons is with <dn>את</dn> <dn>You</dn>, <dn>You</dn> have made his laws, and he does not pass over. [6] Look away from him and let him rest, till like a hired man he enjoys his day. [7] For there is expectancy for a tree, if it is cut down, that it does sprout again, and that its tender branch does not cease. [8] Though its root grows old in the earth, and its stump dies in the ground, [9] at the scent of water it buds and brings forth foliage like a plant. [10] But man dies and is powerless, and man expires, and where is he? [11] Water disappears from the sea, and a river dries up and is parched, [12] and man shall lie down and not rise. Till the heavens are no more, they awake not, nor are aroused from their sleep. [13] If only <dn>You</dn> would hide me in She’ol, conceal me until <dn>Your</dn> wrath turns away. Set for me a law, and remember me! [14] If a man dies, would he live again? All the days of my struggle I wait, till my change comes. [15] <dn>You</dn> would call, and I would answer <dn>You</dn>. <dn>You</dn> have yearned for the work of <dn>Your</dn> hands. [16] For now <dn>You</dn> count my steps – do <dn>You</dn> not watch over my sin? [17] My transgression is sealed up in a bag, and <dn>You</dn> cover over my crookedness. [18] But a falling mountain crumbles away, and a rock is moved from its place, [19] as water wears away stones, its outpouring washes away the soil of the earth – so <dn>You</dn> have destroyed the expectancy of man. [20] <dn>You</dn> overpower him, forever, and he is gone – his face changes and <dn>You</dn> send him away. [21] His sons come to esteem, and he does not know it. And they are brought low, and he does not perceive it. [22] He feels only the pain of his flesh, and he mourns over himself.”

readings.title: The Retributive Philosophy
readings.subtitle: Eliphaz Defends the Penal System
readings.text: [Job 15:1] And Eliphaz the Těmanite answered and said, [2] “Would a wise man answer with vain knowledge, or fill his belly with the east wind? [3] Would he reason with useless talk, or by speeches with which do not profit? [4] Indeed, you do away with reverence, and withhold prayer before <dn>Ěl</dn>. [5] For your crookedness teaches your mouth what to say, and you choose the tongue of the crafty. [6] Not I, but your own mouth condemns you. And your own lips witness against you. [7] Were you the first one born? Or were you made before the hills? [8] Have you heard the secret counsel of <dn>Eloah</dn>? And do you limit wisdom to yourself? [9] What do you know that we do not know – understand, that is not within us? [10] Both the grey-haired and the aged are among us, much older than your father. [11] Are the comforts of <dn>Ěl</dn> not enough for you – and a word that deals gently with you? [12] What have you taken to heart? And why do your eyes flash? [13] That you should turn your spirit against <dn>Ěl</dn>, and let such words go out of your mouth? [14] What is man, that he should be clean? And one born of a woman, that he should be righteous? [15] Look, <dn>He</dn> puts no trust in <dn>His</dn> set-apart ones, and the heavens are not clean in <dn>His</dn> eyes, [16] how much less one who is loathsome and corrupt, drinking unrighteousness like water! [17] Let me show you – hear me – and this I have seen and declare, [18] which the wise declare, and have not hidden from their fathers, [19] to them alone the land was given, and no stranger passed over into their midst: [20] All the days of the wrong one he is paining himself, and few years have been stored up for the ruthless. [21] A frightening sound is in his ears; in peace a destroyer comes to him. [22] He believes not to return from darkness, and he is reserved for the sword. [23] He wanders about for food – where is it? He knows that a day of darkness is prepared for him. [24] Distress and pain frighten him – they overwhelm him, like a sovereign ready for the attack. [25] Because he has stretched out his hand against <dn>Ěl</dn>, and acts mightily against the <dn>Almighty</dn>. [26] He runs against <dn>Him</dn> defiantly, with thick-bossed shields. [27] For he has covered his face with his fatness, and he has put layers of fat on his loins. [28] But he dwells in ruined cities, in houses which no one lives in, which have been ready to become heaps. [29] He shall not be rich, and his wealth shall not rise, and his possessions shall not overspread the earth. [30] He does not turn away from darkness. The flame dries up his branches, and he turns aside by the breath of <dn>His</dn> mouth. [31] Let him not trust in falsehood, deceiving himself, for falsehood is his reward. [32] Before his day it is accomplished, and his branch shall not be green. [33] He shakes off his unripe grape like a vine, and throws off his blossom like an olive tree. [34] For the company of the defiled ones is barren, and fire consumes the tents of bribery. [35] They conceive trouble and bring forth wickedness, even their womb prepares deception.”

readings.title: The Ultimate Injustice
readings.subtitle: Job Appeals to the Heavenly Defender
readings.text: [Job 16:1] And Iyoḇ answered and said, [2] “I have heard many matters like these; all of you are comforters of trouble! [3] Is there an end to words of wind? Or what provokes you that you answer? [4] I might also speak like you, if you were in my place. I might heap up words against you, and shake my head at you. [5] I might strengthen you with my mouth, and my moving lips might bring relief. [6] If I speak, my pain is not relieved; and if I refrain, does it leave me? [7] But now <dn>He</dn> has wearied me. <dn>You</dn> have stunned all my company. [8] And <dn>You</dn> have plucked me, and it is a witness. And my failure rises up against me, it bears witness to my face. [9] <dn>He</dn> has torn in <dn>His</dn> wrath, and <dn>He</dn> hates me. <dn>He</dn> has gnashed at me with <dn>His</dn> teeth; my adversary sharpens <dn>His</dn> eyes upon me. [10] They open wide their mouths at me, in scorn they have stricken my cheeks, they mass themselves together against me. [11] <dn>Ěl</dn> has handed me over to the perverse, and cast me into the hands of the wrong. [12] I was at ease, but <dn>He</dn> broke me. And <dn>He</dn> took me by my neck and shattered me, and <dn>He</dn> has set me up for <dn>His</dn> target. [13] <dn>His</dn> archers surround me, <dn>He</dn> splits my kidneys in two and does not spare, <dn>He</dn> pours out my bile on the ground. [14] <dn>He</dn> made a breach in me, breach upon breach. <dn>He</dn> runs upon me like a mighty man. [15] I sewed sackcloth over my skin, and laid my horn in the dust. [16] My face is reddened from weeping, and on my eyelids is the shadow of death; [17] though no violence was on my hand, and my prayer sincere. [18] O earth, do not cover my blood, and let my cry have no resting place! [19] See, even now my witness is in the heavens, and my defender is on high. [20] My friends are they that scorn me; my eyes pour out tears to <dn>Eloah</dn>. [21] O that one might plead for a man with <dn>Eloah</dn>, as a man with his neighbour! [22] When a few years are past, then I shall go the way of no return.
